transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-10
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Rajesh Kumar (Aegis Head of ML), Sofia Martinez (Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (CTO)

Summary:
Short discovery focused on latency SLOs and throughput targets for a customer considering Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private Redwood deployments. Main asks: p95 latency target ~<350ms for ~512 tokens streamed, concurrency ~50, need streaming and token/sec benchmarks and SOC2 + VPC network requirements. Action items and benchmark run scheduled.

Topics:
- Current infra and model footprint
- p95 SLO targets and warm/cold behavior
- Concurrency and batching expectations
- Streaming vs non-streaming behavior and token/sec perf
- Dedicated 8-GPU pool sizing and cost tradeoffs
- Security (SOC2 / VPC / KMS)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, this is Maya from Redwood, I have Ethan with me, our SE, and we thought we'd run through your latency and throughput goals and then map to hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:12] Rajesh Kumar: Great thanks, Maya. Yeah we— we have pretty tight p95 targets for our product, we want sub 350ms 95th for responses that are around 400–600 tokens, and that's with streaming enabled since our UI renders as tokens come in.
[00:25] Ethan Ross: Okay good, that's helpful. Quick clarification - are you measuring p95 from client-to-client or just inference?
[00:33] Sofia Martinez: We measure end-to-end from our app to the user. So network + app + inference but we can instrument to break out inference-only if needed. Primarily we want guaranteed tail behavior so we can design UX accordingly.
[00:44] Liam O'Connor: And we have peak concurrent sessions of about 50 active generation requests, sustained for maybe 10 minutes during load spikes, the average prompt length is 120 tokens but final responses we stream up to ~512 tokens.
[00:58] Ethan Ross: Got it. So two axes—peak concurrency 50 and p95 <350ms for ~512 token streamed responses. That is aggressive but potentially doable depending on model size, quantization, and whether KV cache warm-up is accounted for.
[01:15] Rajesh Kumar: We're currently running an open Llama variant tuned for safety, about 13B dense. We might switch to a smaller distilled 7B for some routes. We need to understand performance on both.
[01:26] Maya Patel: Perfect, this is the kind of info we need. Quick high-level: hosted is easiest to start and we can usually meet latency for smaller models with our autoscaling and batching knobs; dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, and private/VPC gives you the network control and audit logs you need for compliance.
[01:42] Sofia Martinez: Is there an easy way to compare token/sec numbers between hosted and dedicated? We want to understand cost tradeoffs too.
[01:49] Ethan Ross: Yes — we provide benchmark scripts that measure tokens/sec and end-to-end latencies for streaming and non-streaming. For example, on an 8xA100 dedicated pool with quantized 13B you might see X tokens/sec and p95 latencies around Y for particular prompt lengths — we'll supply exact numbers after we run with your workload.
[02:08] Rajesh Kumar: When you say p95 around Y, can you give a ballpark? We need the ballpark to know if the architecture is feasible.
[02:14] Ethan Ross: Ballpark: for a 13B quantized to int8 on 8xA100 with efficient kernels and streaming, expect sub-second p95 for 512 tokens, but getting down to 350ms p95 for 512 tokens is tough unless you use a smaller model or reduce per-token compute via faster kernels / optimized compilation. The other lever is concurrency: if each request ties up the GPU for long, you need more GPUs to keep end-to-end latency low.
[02:39] Maya Patel: Also worth calling out prefix caching / KV cache is important for chat scenarios — if you can reuse context across requests, effective tokens/sec improves and tail decreases.
[02:48] Liam O'Connor: We do reuse context for session flows about 60% of the time, but new chats are common.
[02:54] Ethan Ross: Ok that's helpful. For new chats we can't rely on cache, so benchmark will include cold KV behavior. We'll measure cold vs warm p95.
[03:05] Rajesh Kumar: About streaming — does Redwood stream tokens as they are generated, or is there buffering that could add latency? We saw product notes about continuous batching, curious about tradeoffs.
[03:14] Ethan Ross: We support real streaming with chunked responses; however continuous batching can introduce micro-batching latency. Our runtime has knobs: you can prioritize latency (flush on single request) or throughput (wait to batch). For p95 goals you'll set the low-latency policy and potentially lower batch windows.
[03:30] Sofia Martinez: Any numbers on the cost impact of turning batching down? Like how much more compute we'd pay per token?
[03:36] Maya Patel: Roughly speaking, pure latency-first runs cost more per token—because you can't amortize across tokens/requests—but we can model it in the spreadsheet. Historically customers see anywhere from 10–50% higher cost per token depending on load shape. We'll put conservative ranges.
[03:51] Rajesh Kumar: For Dedicated, what's the minimum we should consider to hit these p95s at concurrency 50?
[03:57] Ethan Ross: My initial estimate: for a 13B model aiming for low p95 on 512 tokens with streaming and concurrency 50, an 8-GPU A100 pool is a reasonable starting point but I suspect you'd still need tight kernel tuning and prioritization. If you switch to the 7B distill for the critical low-latency route, you could do with 4 GPUs. We need to run your exact prompts to be precise.
[04:18] Liam O'Connor: Hmm, 8 GPUs is within our budget for Dedicated if it meets SLOs. How do failovers work — if one GPU goes down do requests queue?
[04:27] Ethan Ross: Our orchestration supports automatic routing away from unhealthy nodes; there's also overflow to hosted or lower-tier models as a fallback. That said failover will impact latency while redistribution happens. We recommend canary capacity for high-availability.
[04:40] Rajesh Kumar: Can you do region-aware routing? Our users are global so p95 varies a lot by region.
[04:46] Maya Patel: Yes, routing by region is built-in — hosted has multi-region endpoints and Dedicated can be deployed in specific regions. We also support policy-based routing to cheaper regions with fallback.
[04:55] Sofia Martinez: On security, we need SOC2 type 2, SSO/SAML, KMS for keys, and VPC peering. Can Redwood Dedicated/Private support HSM or customer-managed keys?
[05:06] Maya Patel: Yes, Private and Dedicated have KMS integrations and Private can be configured for HSM. We'll share SOC2 docs and the network diagrams in the follow up.
[05:13] Rajesh Kumar: Good. Also can you instrument token-level cost and latency? We want per-route dashboards.
[05:19] Ethan Ross: Yep that’s part of Redwood Console — per-model/per-route token metrics and p95/latency trimming. You can also set alerts on regressions tied to prompt sets.
[05:27] Liam O'Connor: Let's talk about benchmarks — what do you need from us to run a representative one?
[05:32] Ethan Ross: We'll need sample prompt sets representing cold and warm scenarios, traffic shape (concurrency curve), and access to a small VPN/VPC endpoint for private tests if we run in your environment. Otherwise we can run in a mirrored Redwood environment. Also we need to know whether to include streaming latencies measured at 1st token and full response completion.
[05:49] Sofia Martinez: We'll provide prompts and a sample of telemetry logs. We want streaming-first performance (i.e., time to first token p95 <= 120ms ideally) and full response p95 <=350ms. 
[05:59] Maya Patel: That's a helpful split — we'll run both 1st-token and completion p95. Note first-token is heavily impacted by network and warmness; completion p95 scales with total token compute.
[06:09] Rajesh Kumar: For the benchmark harness, can you include autoregressive token/sec numbers and a streaming trace?
[06:15] Ethan Ross: Yes, benchmark will produce tokens/sec, per-token latency, p95-first-token, p95-completion, and CPU/GPU utilization traces. We'll attach those to the benchmark spreadsheet.
[06:25] Sophia Martinez: small nit — we've seen weird naming in transcripts before, will you make sure the benchmark labels models correctly? We have multiple internal versions of the 13B.
[06:32] Ethan Ross: We'll tag by git hash and model binary name in the report.
[06:36] Rajesh Kumar: Cost side — can you show hosted vs dedicated per-token cost and also a committed pricing option?
[06:43] Maya Patel: Absolutely. We'll provide estimated per-token and per-month committed numbers for Dedicated, plus hosted on-demand for the same workload. We'll also include burst and autoscale options.
[06:55] Liam O'Connor: One more technical: do you support model quantization in a way that speeds up streaming vs just final throughput?
[07:01] Ethan Ross: Yes, quantization reduces per-token compute and improves tokens/sec. For streaming it's helpful too because per-token generation is faster. We also have kernel-level optimizations and compilation for attention that affect latency. We'll capture quantized vs FP16 numbers in the benchmark.
[07:15] Rajesh Kumar: Are there any limitations on concurrent streaming connections per node?
[07:20] Ethan Ross: There's no hard limit but practical concurrency is gated by GPU memory and scheduler. With our runtime we can multiplex multiple streams on a GPU but if each stream is using long context windows memory becomes the limiting factor.
[07:34] Sofia Martinez: Ok let's outline the follow-ups: schedule the benchmark, send doc pack, and a proposed Dedicated configuration.
[07:41] Maya Patel: Yep, next steps as discussed. I'll send the SLO doc and security pack after the call. Ethan will set up the benchmark harness and we'll loop in Sofia for infra access.
[07:51] Rajesh Kumar: Sounds good, thanks both.
[07:54] Liam O'Connor: Quick question — are there known customers who hit these kinds of p95s with similar models?
[07:59] Maya Patel: Yes, we have customers in e-commerce and search that run 7B/13B and hit sub-second p95s with similar setups; we'll anonymize references and include a short case note.
[08:10] Rajesh Kumar: Great, that will help our internal stakeholders.
[08:13] Maya Patel: Any other questions?
[08:15] Sofia Martinez: One last one on networking — for Private we'd want air-gapped option long-term, is that supported?
[08:21] Ethan Ross: Yes, on-prem air-gapped deployments are supported through our Private offering, though benchmarking in that mode requires a slightly different setup — we'll coordinate.
[08:31] Maya Patel: Alright, quick recap before we close: action items, benchmark run week of 12/13, docs to be shared by 12/11, customer provides prompts and traffic by 12/12.
[08:42] Rajesh Kumar: Confirmed. Thanks everyone.
[08:45] Maya Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with calendar invites. Bye.

End of transcript.
